purpose: Extend original bilingual Week 3 practice and the existing Arcade with bounded noun and verb practice. Private class worksheets and book extracts are not published.

Adjacent present-tense and reflexive revision reviewed to choose prerequisites. Independent homework on pages 3 and 17 was not completed.
Earlier formation and irregular-participle review used to avoid duplicating an entire grammar unit.
Earlier spare-time present-tense material reviewed selectively in the existing page-preserving class extract.
Bounded grammar tables and travel contexts reviewed; pages 45/46/68 and 82/83/84 were checked around booking vocabulary. This is not a new full-book page-by-page review.

findings: Page 7 is an image conjugation table for essere and avere in the passato prossimo.
Page 8 has an overbroad intransitive-verb heading; its activity-verb exceptions require explicitly teaching that not every intransitive or movement verb uses essere.
Page 19 is a reflection graphic, retained as reference with original self-assessment guidance.

baselinePreservation.policy: All prior IDs, object fields, ordering, examples and answers remain unchanged except the three explicitly listed additive grammar mission links.

missionSourceMap.outcome: Contrast ho viaggiato / ho camminato with sono arrivato/a / sono tornato/a in a three-sentence journey.
Use letto, scritto, preso and fatto in short completed-action sentences, including subject changes and time expressions.
Retain the reflexive pronoun, select essere, agree the participle and place non in a morning-routine account.

boosterAuthoring.sourcePolicy: Each entry has exact source page pointers. The catalogue provides original examples and authored conjugation data, derived from reviewed forms and rules; it does not claim that every source prints every six-person form. Book grammar references support regular pattern transfer.
boosterAuthoring.nounPolicy: 32 nouns have explicit grammatical gender, article, plural, original translated example and sources. Collega has separate male and female entries; estetista is explicitly the feminine entry. These curated article cards supplement existing vocabulary banks.
boosterAuthoring.auxiliaryPolicy: The past prompt includes an authored use context. Finire is constrained to finishing il lavoro and uses avere; its note contrasts the intransitive essere use. Conoscere explains getting acquainted in the completed past. Reflexives include their pronoun and use essere.
boosterAuthoring.variantPolicy: Gender-unspecified essere forms accept both masculine and feminine endings; named subjects in authored mission checks disambiguate agreement. Vedere accepts visto and veduto. Accented è remains distinct from e.
boosterAuthoring.scope: 50 selected useful verbs, not an exhaustive course concordance. Modals and ambiguous motion-verb uses such as correre/salire/passare are deliberately not generated from a single auxiliary. No imperfect, remote past or subjunctive claim is made for these drills.

teachingCorrectionsAndChoices: Do not turn the source’s broad intransitive heading into an all-intransitives-use-essere rule. Teach activity counterexamples camminare, nuotare, viaggiare and dormire.
Use contextual subject cues for agreement; do not reject a reasonable gender variant when io/tu/noi/voi/loro does not specify it.
Retain both parts of the passato prossimo and all reflexive pronouns in full-form questions.
Keep original parallel practice separate from the supplied auxiliary worksheet and film homework.
Re-use three existing grammar units instead of introducing near-duplicate units; provide three new five-minute outcomes and six-line guided scenes.
Each new bank contains eight words or chunks. The new course vocabulary is supplemented by common scaffolding such as subito and a piedi in original examples.

scopeLimits: Raw source PDFs, class identities, extracted text, lexical evidence and rendered pages remain ignored private working material.
The external class-video pointer is optional and is not claimed to have been watched or availability-verified.
The 600 generated tense prompts are controlled retrieval practice, not 600 separately authored lessons or evidence of spontaneous speaking mastery.
These content checks do not certify mobile usability, desktop usability, network synchronisation or authentication; those need separate live user-journey audits.
Existing 30–60 minute study scaffolding consumes the new mission, bank and guided-scene data. This content change does not introduce another navigation system.
